claim: 1992 Williams introduced REINFORCE as a family of stochastic weight updates for connectionist networks
notes: Not a modern deep RL benchmark paper.

claim: General form Delta w_ij=alpha_ij(r-b_ij)e_ij; e_ij is the score derivative
notes: Baseline conditionally independent of sampled unit output.

claim: When alpha is shared, expected REINFORCE update equals alpha times gradient of expected reinforcement
notes: Requires hypotheses of theorem, not guarantee of monotonic improvement for every sample.

claim: For Bernoulli logistic units the score derivative is (y_i-p_i)x_j
notes: Special case of original network.

claim: Original episodic REINFORCE uses terminal reinforcement and eligibility summed through time
notes: Distinguish from modern reward-to-go with dense rewards.

claim: Action independent baseline leaves expected policy gradient unchanged
notes: Baseline must not use the sampled action; stop gradients through baseline on actor objective.

claim: Trajectory log probability permits likelihood ratio gradient without differentiating environment transitions
notes: For a finite horizon undiscounted return and theta-independent environment.

claim: Reward-to-go drops rewards from the past in modern VPG derivation
locator: Don't Let the Past Distract You
notes: Monte Carlo return; not bootstrapping.

claim: Policy gradient theorem with function approximation formalizes a larger family after Williams
notes: Do not attribute this theorem to Williams Eq. 11.

claim: Original paper discusses lack of general convergence theory and false optima
notes: Do not claim unconditional convergence.

claim: Two-action bandit with p=.35, r1=2, r0=0 has exact gradient .455 and zero-variance scalar baseline 1.3
notes: Independent teaching calculation; not an original paper result.

claim: Baseline choice can increase variance even while leaving expected gradient invariant
notes: Zero variance arises only in the deterministic two-action toy.

claim: All article diagrams are independently composed conceptual illustrations
notes: Not reproduced figures, experiment curves, or model schematics from paper.

claim: Start-state discounted finite-horizon objective requires absolute gamma^t times relative discounted return
notes: Fixed initial distribution and dynamics; gamma^t can instead be absorbed by sampling weights.

claim: Autoregressive response log probability equals sum of generated token log probabilities
locator: RLHF contextual bandit formulation, Section 2; article Eq. 11
notes: EOS included if sampled; padding and prompt excluded.

claim: Sequence mean of summed logprobs differs from per-response length-normalized objective
notes: No benchmark claim.

claim: RLOO uses other responses as the baseline
notes: Independent sampling conditional on prompt.

claim: Self-inclusive unnormalized group mean scales gradient by (K-1)/K; RLOO corrects that scale
locator: Article Eq. 13; exact enumeration in test_mini_reinforce.py
notes: Fixed individual reward, iid samples, no clipping or standardization.

claim: GRPO includes group relative advantage and PPO-style clipping and reference KL
notes: Outcome variant uses reward standardization; not identical to RLOO.

claim: Full sequence likelihood ratio recovers target-policy expectation if behavior support covers target
notes: Token-local clipping is not exact sequence IS.

claim: For fixed reference, differentiating expected sequence KL yields score times log ratio since expected score is zero
notes: On-policy and regularity conditions; not a claim about any specific KL implementation.

claim: New discount, token, and leave-one-out illustrations are independently composed
notes: No copied paper diagrams or empirical results.
